claims.text: The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi nanoribbons possess intrinsic microstructural disorder.
The nanoribbons experience low-dimensional heat-transfer constraints.
Synchronized microheater pulses will enhance localized thermal gradients at the nanoribbon/substrate interface.
Enhanced localized thermal gradients will lower effective thermal-activation barriers.
Lower effective thermal-activation barriers will make the magnetostructural transition more reversible.
Synchronized microheater pulses will locally adjust temperature during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Local temperature modulation will accelerate heat transfer.
Thermal modulation will overcome intrinsic heat-transfer limitations in the low-dimensional structures.
Thermal modulation will reduce energy barriers for magnetostructural transitions.
Thermal modulation will diminish defect-related domain-wall pinning.
Reduced transition barriers and domain-wall pinning will narrow the magnetic hysteresis loop.
Reduced transition barriers and domain-wall pinning will enhance the magnetocaloric response.
Microheater-equipped devices will exhibit a more pronounced magnetocaloric peak than control nanoribbons without microheaters.
The magnetocaloric peak in microheater-equipped devices will occur closer to ambient temperature.
Microheater-equipped devices will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than baseline nanoribbons without microheaters.
The improvements caused by microheater synchronization will become more significant at higher cycle frequencies.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi baseline nanoribbons exhibit measurable hysteresis.
As-deposited baseline nanoribbons have a limited magnetocaloric response because of low-dimensional heat-transfer constraints.
The proposed mechanism is applicable at magnetic fields of 10–50 mT, heater-pulse durations of 10–100 ms, and cycle frequencies of 1–10 Hz.
The observations may not extend to bulk materials or operation outside the specified field, pulse-duration, and frequency ranges.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says that absence of frequency-dependent magnetocaloric enhancement alone falsifies the hypothesis, whereas the formal rule frames falsification around failure to obtain both a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and an enhanced magnetocaloric response with frequency-dependent behavior. A response could therefore satisfy one rule but not the other.
